input: Volunteer at a local soup kitchen this weekend

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the user wants a one-time shift or the start of a recurring commitment changes how much effort to put into finding the right fit versus the nearest available option.
Whether the user is going alone or with others (friends, family, a group) affects which venues to target, since some soup kitchens have minimum group sizes or require individual registration.
The user's city or neighborhood determines which specific soup kitchens are actually reachable and relevant — without this, no concrete venue can be identified.
Their available hours on Saturday and/or Sunday narrow down which shift slots are feasible — morning, midday, and evening shifts vary widely by location.
Knowing whether the user has already identified a venue or needs help finding one determines the very first action — researching options vs. going straight to registration.
Some people want to serve food directly, others prefer prep work, sorting donations, or other behind-the-scenes roles — this affects which venues or shift types to prioritize.
Understanding what 'done well' means — just showing up, building a relationship with one organization, or gaining a specific experience — shapes how to evaluate and choose between options.

gold.taskTitle: Volunteer at a local soup kitchen this weekend
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to sign up for and show up to a volunteer shift at a nearby soup kitchen within the coming weekend.

questions.title: Is this a one-time shift or start of regular volunteering?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants a single experience this weekend or is looking to begin an ongoing commitment, which changes how selective they should be about finding the best-fit location.

questions.title: What city or neighborhood are you based in?
questions.description: Identify the user's location so that only geographically reachable soup kitchens are surfaced during the research step.

questions.title: Which day and hours are you free this weekend?
questions.description: Pin down the specific windows of availability on Saturday and/or Sunday to match against real shift openings at local venues.

questions.title: Will you be going alone or with other people?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is a solo visit or a group effort, since some organizations require group pre-registration or have minimum/maximum volunteer counts per shift.

questions.title: Do you already have a specific venue in mind?
questions.description: Establish whether the user needs help finding a soup kitchen or has already identified one, so the plan starts at the right step — research vs. direct sign-up.

questions.title: What type of volunteer role appeals most to you?
questions.description: Find out whether the user prefers front-of-house roles like serving or greeting guests, or behind-the-scenes work like food prep or sorting, to help match them to the right shift type.

questions.title: What would make this weekend feel like a success to you?
questions.description: Understand the user's personal measure of success — whether that is simply completing a shift, connecting with an organization long-term, or gaining hands-on experience — to guide decision-making throughout.
